# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Iteration 5/5, final. Parent = `cand_0001` (the champion, val 0.950, 38/40). Three consecutive
rejections precede this one, and all three stamped **`fixed={31628, 80-42}`** — the same two tasks
this candidate targets.

## Headline: the decisive finding this iteration is about MEASUREMENT, not diagnosis

I pivoted per-task reward across all five scored candidates in `.capevolve/run_suite/rollouts/val/`:

| candidate | val | tasks passing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| seed | 0.450 | 18 |
| cand_0001 | **0.950** | 38 |
| cand_0002 | 0.925 | 37 |
| cand_0003 | 0.875 | 35 |
| cand_0004 | 0.925 | 37 |

- **always-pass across all 5 candidates: 16 tasks. always-fail: 0. FLIPPING: 24 of 40.**
- The gate's own rejection lines put `SE = 0.0565`, so `2·SE = 0.113` ≈ **4.5 tasks**. The entire
  spread from cand_0001 (0.950) to cand_0003 (0.875) is 3 tasks — *inside* the resolvable effect.
- `43436` passes in **1 of 5** candidates; `51-12` and `9569` in **2 of 5**; `227-40` and `80-42` in
  3 of 5. These are coin-flips on a single trial per task, not rule-driven regressions.

Consequence for this iteration's strategy: the three `broke` sets in `LEDGER.md` are dominated by
per-task variance, not by mis-firing rules. The way to *gain* is the 2 failing tasks (+0.050); the
way to *lose* is to perturb any of the 24 flip-prone tasks. So this is deliberately a **narrow,
high-confidence** candidate — three edits, each targeting a task failing in THIS iteration's traces,
each with a task-by-task blast radius. I drafted four more, verified them, and then **deleted**
them; that deletion is the main decision of the iteration and is documented below.

**Environment check (explicit):** no environment fault. All 40 traces in `./trajectories/` have
`rollout['error'] == None`, every task executed code and produced an output file, and the two
failures are content-specific (wrong value type; wrong appended row count). Nothing to hand back.

## Ranked issue list — clusters FAILING in this iteration's `./trajectories/`

| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | leverage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A date **component** written as a `datetime` | 31628 | Agent reaches the right reading, then mis-ranks two clauses of the same instruction, and cites the task_template CONTRACT to justify the wrong type | **CONTRACT + CONFLICT** | 1 task = 0.025 |
| 2 | Append sized with `ws.max_row`, inflating it by exactly the formatting-only rows | 80-42 | `range(2, ws_src.max_row + 1)` over sources; the surplus blanks are *interior*, so every later source block sits N rows low | **KNOWLEDGE** | 1 task = 0.025 |

That is the complete list. 38 of 40 tasks score exactly 1.0; I read every `score.feedback` string,
not only the two failures, and there is no partial-credit, omission or communication cluster hiding
behind a 1.0. Max headroom this iteration is **+0.050**.

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit)

| cluster | edit class (skill lever) | file | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 / 31628 | **consolidate a conflicting rule + add an example** (levers 3 + 5) | `prompt.md` §1(b) | Replaces cand_0001's "a date **part** is that component as a small integer" sentence with a **precedence** rule: the clause naming *what to extract* fixes the type; a later "display the resulting **date**" / "show the result" / "as a static number" says only *where* the value goes or *how* it is stored and cannot re-type it. `datetime` only when no component is named anywhere. One worked example on invented cells (`ws["F1"] = 27`). General: a property of how these user-written instructions restate themselves, no task id, target or answer | YES — bounded, and it *narrows* nothing that was permitted |
| 1 / 31628 | **tighten the output contract where it is actually cited** (lever 8) | `task_template.md` CONTRACT item 2 | Scopes "dates as `datetime`" to an answer that *is* a date; it does not govern a number the instruction asks you to take *out* of a date | YES — narrows a clause the passing tasks already satisfy |
| 1 / 31628 | **add a sourced tie-break at the point of use** (lever 4) | `task_template.md` Phase 1 | Gated on "When **no** cell in the file can break the tie": rank the clauses by role, not by which reads more confidently; "calling one of them 'explicit' is not evidence" | YES — conditional, fires only after the file-evidence test fails |
| 2 / 80-42 | **add a rule the source requires + a copyable procedure** (levers 4 + 5) | `prompt.md` §4 | Take each source's row count from its declared `[data extent]`, never `ws.max_row`; print `max_row` vs `data rows` per source and reconcile the total before writing. Carries an explicit carve-out: governs the **source-read** loop only, never which rows you write | YES — bounded; provably a no-op on the one passing task it can fire on |

All four hunks are additive or narrowing. None loosens a permission, none adds a step every task
must run, and none deletes text — except the single sentence Edit 1 **replaces**, whose constraint
survives (stronger) inside the new bullet. That matters: `LEDGER.md` shows cand_0003 is the only
batch that pruned and the only one that broke 395-36/48527/9569.

## Verify-the-fix, and blast radius, one block per change

### Edit 1+2+3 — the 31628 type-precedence cluster

**Why it is not a knowledge gap.** `cand_0001` *already contained* the date-part rule, and 31628
still wrote a `datetime` — scorer: *"1 cell(s) hold datetime where int was expected"*. Its own trace
shows it found both readings and ranked them wrongly: *"'Number of the last day' is slightly
ambiguous, but 'resulting date' is explicit."* The missing element is a **tie-break between two
clauses of one instruction**, which Edit 1 states and Edit 3 places in the procedure at the exact
point the agent chooses.

**Why the fix has to live in `task_template.md` too.** The same trace justifies the wrong type by
quoting the other file: *"the CONTRACT requires dates to be written as datetime objects."* Two prior
iterations strengthened `prompt.md` §1(b) and left that CONTRACT sentence unqualified, so the
contradiction survived and the agent kept citing the CONTRACT over the system prompt. A stronger
rule elsewhere cannot beat the rule being cited; the cited sentence must be narrowed. That is Edit 2.

**Confirmed effective:** three framework RESULT stamps (cand_0002, cand_0003, cand_0004) all list
`fixed={31628, 80-42}` with this rule present in some form.

**Blast radius: BOUNDED.** Of the 38 passing instructions, exactly **1** names a date component
(43436 — where the phrase is a filter boundary, and which already writes `int`). The only **2**
passing tasks that write a `datetime` into a graded cell, **9726** and **416-15**, name no component
anywhere, so they land on the rule's explicit fallback ("write a `datetime` only when no component is
named"); I read both traces directly rather than inferring. Grepped all 40 traces for `1899,12,30`
/ `toordinal` / `serial_number`: **zero hits**, so no passing answer is an Excel serial.

### Edit 4 — the 80-42 append-sizing cluster

**Evidence is the task's own stdout.** Declared extents are Jack 1-2000, Henry 1-1000, Richard
1-1001 → 3998 data rows; Consolidate_ALL extends to 3999 and the trace printed `First blank row:
4000` and `Last row: 8997`. 4998 rows appended, **1000 too many** — exactly one source's
formatting-only rows. Those blanks are *interior*, so every later source block sat 1000 rows low:
the scorer reports 84986 of 95988 cells filled, with values that were each **copied correctly** but
compared against the wrong record. Confirmed effective by the same three RESULT stamps.

**Blast radius: BOUNDED, by regex over all 40 instructions.** Only **2 of 40** match an
append/consolidate trigger: 80-42 (failing) and **402-43** (passing). On 402-43 the rule is a
verified **no-op** — its sheet's declared extent is `rows 1-25` and its trace prints `max_row` 25,
so `data rows == max_row` and the filter removes nothing; it also writes to a freshly created
Sheet2. The 2 passing tasks where `max_row` exceeds the declared extent (**37378, 382-10**) have no
append trigger, so the rule cannot fire on them. **395-36**, which must *emit* near-empty output
rows, is protected by the carve-out sentence. I audited every passing trace that touches `max_row`
(25 of them): each one that uses it on the write path already guards with a `None` test on a key
column, so the rule is value-neutral there.

### Contract safety (checked explicitly, because breaking it zeroes all 40)

Simulated the harness's `.format()` on the edited `task_template.md`: all six required placeholders
(`{instruction}` `{spreadsheet_path}` `{spreadsheet_content}` `{instruction_type}`
`{answer_position}` `{output_path}`) plus the optional `{max_turns}` substitute cleanly, no invented
placeholders, no stray single braces. Renders to 9852 chars. `diff -u` against
`candidates/cand_0001/` confirms exactly the four intended hunks and no other text change. Total
size 27134 B vs parent 24345 B (+2.8 KB), comparable to cand_0004's 26635 B.

## Deliberately skipped — and why (the main decision of this iteration)

I drafted, wrote into the files, verified, and then **removed** four further edits. Each is real in
*some* candidate's traces, but each fails the **REAL** test here: its target task **passes** in this
iteration's `./trajectories/`. Fixing a currently-passing task buys no headroom and spends blast
radius on precisely the flip-prone set.

1. **Header-row / first-data-row detection** (per-sheet, "never assume row 2"). Targets 395-36's
   dropped ID, 227-40's dropped header, 9569's wrong start column — **all three pass here**. A
   subagent audit also found 9 passing tasks whose header sits below row 1 (9569's is at row 8), so
   the rule as drafted was incomplete for exactly the layouts it would newly govern.
2. **Worked-example rule** — "reproduce the example by COMPUTING it, never by whitelisting its
   values and never by rounding to match its displayed precision". Targets 48527's value whitelist
   and 9569's `round(v, 4)`; **both pass here**. Also in mild tension with the existing
   preservation rule, which tells the agent to leave those cells alone.
3. **Empty-named-source-range rule** (an empty range named as a READ SOURCE describes the asker's
   own larger workbook). Targets 51-12 — **passes here**. A subagent showed the first draft would
   have flipped 5 passing tasks (227-40, 53647, 37456, 560-12, 463-17) whose instruction names an
   empty range that is the *write target*. I added a carve-out and it was still out of scope.
4. **Discriminating-calibration rule** ("calibrate at a parameter where the two readings actually
   differ"). Genuinely interesting — Phase 1b has **never once executed as code in any of the 40
   traces**, so it is currently decorative — but its target (43436) passes here, and the wording sat
   close to cand_0003's anti-relitigation clause, which the cross-rejection diff identifies as the
   mechanism that licensed skipping Phase 1b. Not worth it on the last iteration.

I also **refuted two hypotheses before they became edits**, which is why they are absent:

- *"Multi-`python`-block replies get silently dropped after the first, discarding calibration
  code."* Only the first block runs — but **24 of 38 passing tasks emit multi-block replies and pass
  anyway**, and only 1 of the 2 failures does. Refuted; no edit.
- *"A repetition stall burns the round budget."* 51-12 re-sent an identical block 13 times under
  cand_0002 — but in **this** candidate's 40 traces, no trace re-sends its executed block across
  rounds and no tool output repeats. Not a defect of the current champion; no edit.

## Why not more edits, given the instruction to maximise breadth

Breadth is the right default and I would normally ship all seven. Recording the reasoning because it
cuts against the brief: with 38/40 passing there are only two clusters, so "as many fixes as
possible" has a hard ceiling of two clusters' worth of edits. Past that ceiling, every extra edit is
pure downside against 24 tasks that flip on their own. Three consecutive rejections each landed
their intended fixes and were sunk purely by 3–5 flip-prone tasks moving. **Breadth means cover
every real cluster, not produce N edits.**

## Process & features used

- **Parallel read-only `Explore` fan-out (4 agents):** (a) 43436's cross-candidate divergence,
  (b) the other five tasks in prior `broke` sets, (c) worked-example blast radius over all 38
  passing tasks, (d) header-row + empty-range blast radius. Their per-task verdicts are why edits
  1–4 shipped and the other four did not.
- **Subagent reports are hypotheses.** I re-derived every load-bearing number myself: the flip
  matrix, the 402-43 no-op, 80-42's 3998-vs-4998 arithmetic, and the multi-block refutation.
- **Prior iterations read in full:** `RUNMAP.md`, `prior_iterations/cand_0002|0003|0004/` (PROCESS +
  `diff.patch`), `LEDGER.md`, `JOURNAL.md`, `INSIGHTS.md`, `META_INSIGHTS.md`, and
  `rejected.jsonl`. This candidate is structurally different from all three rejects: it adds **no**
  mandatory step to the shared Phase-1/Phase-3 procedure (cand_0002, cand_0004), deletes nothing
  (cand_0003), and contains no anti-relitigation clause (cand_0003).
- **No edit to any adapter, harness, scorer, benchmark or environment file, and no shell command
  that mutates the environment.** Only `prompt.md`, `task_template.md` and the handover docs.

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)

- §1(a) "a formula is not an answer — write the computed literal", including *"even when the
  instruction says 'formula'"*. Largest measured win (~11 tasks); the instructions actively bait the
  agent into breaking it.
- The **conditional** phrasing of the preserve-the-workbook rule in §4. Never promote it to a blanket
  openpyxl mandate: 13 of 18 originally-passing tasks win via `pandas.to_excel`.
- The Phase 3 stop condition and the "reply with **no code block**" wording. That, not the output
  file's existence, is what terminates the loop; 20 of 40 seed tasks burned ~28 rounds without it.
- §5's `dropna` bullet and §4's "either approach works" opener — the only batch that removed them is
  the only batch that broke 395-36/48527/9569.
